The library was quiet, save for the faint hum of the fluorescent lights overhead. I sat at a wooden table, surrounded by stacks of dusty tomes and scattered notes. The air was thick with the scent of old books and stale coffee.

I stared at the back of the book in front of me, the dog-eared pages fluttering in the gentle breeze from the air vent. My mind wandered to the words etched on the cover: A Brief History of Obscure Inventions.

As I delved deeper into the narrative, I found myself entwined in the tale of a 19th-century inventor who had dedicated his life to creating a machine capable of bending the fabric of time and space. The words danced on the page, hypnotic and alluring, drawing me in with an otherworldly allure.

The inventor, a man named Ezra Foster, had been driven mad by his own ambitions. He spent years pouring over mathematical equations, testing his contraptions on unsuspecting laboratory assistants. The public thought him a charlatan, a swindler peddling impossibility to the gullible masses.

But I knew the truth.

As I read on, I felt the boundaries between reality and fantasy blurring. I became Ezra Foster, eyes fixed on a distant horizon, fueled by a burning zealousness that defied reason. The world around me melted away, leaving only the tunnel-vision focus of creation.

Ezra's machines multiplied in my mind, each one a Most Humble Servant of the Grand Design. They burst from the pages of the book, ratcheting up the momentum of the narrative. The dates and times began to blur, leaving only an impulse, a seconds-removed feeling of universe-bending optimalism.

As I gazed deeper into the text, a latent dimension revealed itself – a locus of clustered might, concatenating every force in the universe. Foster was the master architect, legislating time and motion, imbuing the stories of those within and around him with an aesthetic glimpse of keystone truth.

Suddenly, the surrounding silence became oppressive. I became acutely aware of my own breathing, the weight of my hands resting upon the tabletop. Or.

Words ceased.

I don't know which.

Because in that moment, all became clear.
